start.text: The bramble wall stands higher than your head: canes as thick as a thumb, arched over and over each other, thorns as long as a finger. A few hips hang on it, red as coals.
The cart road's ruts run straight in under the canes. They do not come out on the other side, as far as you can see.
On a pine beside it, a cutter has cut the camp's notch for "this way home". It points into the thorns.
Your ember leans toward the brambles, very slightly, the way the Gull's cradle once leaned toward it.

choice.text: Hold the ember to the thorns.

part.text: You hold out your hand. The nearest canes draw back from the ember the way a hand draws back from a stove: slowly, then all at once.
Thorns unhook from thorns. A gap opens, the width of one person, and the cart road's ruts run on through it into grey.
Behind you, at the camp, somebody has stopped sawing.

again.text: The canes lift away from your ember as you come near, thorns unhooking from thorns, and the gap opens again onto the grey road.

not_yet.text: You lower your hand. The canes settle back over the gap, thorn by thorn, unhurried.
